title: Injury Q&A #2
summary: NH answers viewer injury questions: trap imbalance from one-strap backpacks, low back pain after squats, pulling from blocks, hip and glute pain, ankle injuries, quad versus hamstring balance, twitching, and benching after shoulder surgery. His recurring advice is to keep moving pain-free, find the least painful variation, rebuild form with light weight, and use weighted stretches.
claims: Injury prevention is critical because injury stops training and causes muscle loss
Carrying a backpack on one shoulder while still growing can create scoliosis; he believes his own scoliosis came from that
Trap imbalance from scoliosis has a structural part that cannot be corrected once bones are set, and a tension part from constant shrugging that can
Constantly remind yourself to keep the shoulders back and down; posture influences structure and vice versa
Barbell weighted stretches for the traps, with slight shoulder angle changes, can load one trap more and relieve trap tightness
He used to have painful knots in his traps; they disappeared after he started weighted stretches, with none in 5-6 months
Most suspected lower back injuries are actually SI joint, nerve or muscle issues; discs are hard to destroy
After a low back tweak, keep moving: unweighted good mornings and squats with manageable pain; stopping completely does not help
Ice and contrast showers aimed at the low back can help recovery
Find a lower body movement you can do pain-free (leg press, good morning), then return to squats and deadlifts with low weight
Rebuild squat form after a back injury to find the torso position that irritates the lower back least
Squats cause more lower back injuries than deadlifts; the most dangerous part of any lower body lift (except good mornings) is reversing out of the bottom of the squat
Paused squats with low weight help diagnose how the back reacts out of the hole
Back hyperextensions are excellent for the lower back and teach pulling and pushing with the legs
Daily dead hangs after workouts help decompress the spine
Core is protected by proper bracing and strong abs; leg raises, hanging leg raises, planks and incline crunches build it, but cannot fix a current back injury
Training only partial ranges (block pulls, half-rep bench) then suddenly going full range heavy is when people snap pecs or backs
If you pull from blocks, do max work off blocks and submaximal work from the floor to build range safely
Tall lifters who cannot pull from the floor anthropometrically should not be ashamed of pulling from blocks or a rack
Recurring training pain either disappears on its own or gradually worsens as a warning; it rarely just stays the same
For hip pain on deadlifts, pause deadlifts, train the least painful lower body movement up, then reintroduce squats and later deadlifts
Stretch tight hips after workouts when warm, never cold
Heavier people's ankle injuries can last months because bodyweight keeps straining them; avoid high-impact sports
Ice an injured joint 3-4 times a day for 15 minutes, then stay still the same duration
At 240 lb his rolled ankle would not heal; at 220 lb it healed quickly, so losing weight can help
Quad training itself does not cause knee injuries; problems arise when tendon fatigue outpaces muscle recovery
Injuries come from poor technique, poor volume and intensity management and overall muscle weakness, not from one dominant muscle
Most lifters should do more hip hinge than knee flexion because naturals almost always end up quad-dominant
He was quad-dominant with weak hamstrings and is slowly correcting it
Glute injuries on squats come from staying too vertical without hip hinging, so the glutes are recruited all at once at the bottom
Rehab glutes with hip thrusts, glute bridges and hyperextensions at low intensity; put strength goals aside while injured
Light RDLs and good mornings with slow negatives stretch the glute and help locate the painful range
Tweak stance and torso angle only with light weights, never at high intensity
Muscle twitching is harmless, often low magnesium or potassium or dehydration
After shoulder surgery, avoid touch-and-go bench; use slingshot, close-grip, paused bench or Spoto press, or push-ups and ring push-ups
Tight shoulders come from a tight scapular girdle or overdeveloped front delts; weighted stretch and face pulls help
He does not give advice on severe or surgery-related injuries beyond his expertise
He takes MSM powder for joints
Elbow pain on fast full extension sounds like tendinitis
exercises: adjust shoulder angle to bias one side
diagnose back pain out of the hole
max off blocks, submax from floor
